editorial.headline: Professional Judges and Referees: Open Nationally, Closed to Bali PMA
editorial.standfirst: Nationally, this individual professional activity permits full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s registration structure prevents a PT PMA from entering it today.
editorial.body:
This activity covers professional judges and referees who act in an individual capacity. The operative idea is personal professional officiating: the code is about the work done by a judge or referee, carried out in that person’s own capacity. That makes the scope deliberately specific. The record identifies a professional role, the two forms of officiating it includes, and the individual basis on which that role is performed. For founders, the useful starting point is therefore the activity itself: professional judging and refereeing, registered on an individual footing.

Scale is not a side note in this record; it defines the available registration range. The open scales are Mikro, Kecil, and Menengah. Put plainly, the listed route is for micro, small, and medium enterprises. The absence of an Usaha Besar scale row becomes consequential in Bali, but even before reaching the regional picture it signals that this is not presented as an unrestricted, all-scale activity. A founder should read the scale list alongside the scope: it is a tightly framed professional activity with access specified at the micro, small, and medium levels.

Nationally, the investment position is unequivocally open. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, which means the national record permits full foreign ownership of this activity. That is a meaningful national fact, not a hint at a partial foreign stake: the stated ceiling is complete ownership. But a national ceiling answers only the national ownership question. It does not, on its own, establish that the activity can be registered through every regional route. Bali supplies the decisive qualification—and it is a hard one.

In Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity through a PT PMA today. The Bali status is CHIUSO_PMA_NO_BESAR because OSS has no Usaha Besar scale row; the activity is reserved for UMKM, while a PT PMA is Usaha Besar by law and cannot register. The record also notes Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocking PMA registration for its stated low and medium-low risk categories. The conclusion needs no softening: 100% national foreign ownership remains the national position, yet it creates no Bali PT PMA registration route for this activity.
